raw.thesis: Narma addresses the challenge of scaling AI automation within AI-first companies by providing an "Enterprise Agentic Brain." This venture aims to solve the problem of identifying high-ROI automation opportunities, measuring their impact, and continuously adapting AI agents to evolving work patterns. The core innovation lies in its three-layer architecture: observing work patterns via desktop sensors, intelligently identifying intent and value, and autonomously generating and deploying AI agents. Narma does not build its own LLMs but leverages existing foundation models, focusing instead on understanding the "Work Graph" to pinpoint inefficiencies and automate tasks mid-flow. The target user is an AI-first company struggling to effectively deploy and measure AI automation. The founder envisions a continuous AI optimization loop, suggesting a growth startup trajectory. Currently, the venture is at the idea stage, with the concept fully articulated but no mention of development or user acquisition.
raw.what_makes_this_different: Narma differentiates itself by focusing on the "Work Graph" to precisely identify automation opportunities and by autonomously generating and deploying AI agents, leveraging existing foundation models instead of building its own.
raw.core_excitement: The founder is excited by the prospect of a single system that can continuously observe work, decide optimal AI interventions, and automatically build agents for "Continuous AI lift."

core_insight.if_wrong: If Narma cannot accurately identify high-ROI opportunities or effectively generate and deploy agents, then companies will not see a measurable return on their AI automation efforts.
core_insight.why_different: Narma focuses on observing the 'Work Graph' to identify where AI can intercept work mid-flow and autonomously generates custom agents, rather than building foundational models or relying on manual identification of automation opportunities.
